newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GARTNER CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY EARLY WITH OVERTIME GOAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GARTNER CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY EARLY WITH OVERTIME GOAL.

text.p: Seemingly ageless wonder Mike Gartner celebrated his birthday a day early Monday by scoring his league-leading 10th goal 1:45 into overtime to lift the Phoenix Coyotes to a 5-4 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.
The winning goal was the second of the game for Gartner, the fifth all-time leading goal scorer in the National Hockey League who turns 37 Tuesday.
"I guess I found new life in the spring," said Gartner, after his 1,300th career game. "I didn't know where the puck was going. I just shot at the net."

It appeared as if the Coyotes would end their five-game winless streak in regulation when Dallas Drake fed Craig Janney from behind the net with 2:11 left in the third period and Janney beat Pat Jablonski for a 4-3 lead.
But Montreal pulled the goalie for an extra attacker and it paid off when Mark Recchi beat Darcy Wakaluk with a low slap shot from 30 feet out with 24 seconds left to force overtime.
In overtime, an open Gartner took a pass from Darrin Shannon from the corner and the future Hall of Famer got off a shot from 30 feet out that sailed past Jablonski.
"Gartner's shot was very strange," Jablonski said of the overtime goal. "It floated at me. I waved at it and somehow it got by me."
Gartner's first goal of the game, a powerplay tally, had tied the game 2-2 at 3:56 of the second period.
Recchi had two goals and an assist for the Canadiens. Pierre Turgeon assisted on all four goals for Montreal, which lost at home for the first time this season.
At Colorado, All-Star goaltender Patrick Roy got the night off and in his place Craig Billington made 40 saves to record his sixth career shutout as the Avalanche edged the Washington Capitals 1-0.
Valeri Kamensky scored the game's only goal 70 seconds into the second period for the Stanley Cup champions.
Kamensky took a pass from Peter Forsberg, skated in from the blue line and fired a shot from the left circle that beat Olaf Kolzig to his right.
Kolzig stopped 33 shots in a fine effort for the Caps.
Billington was playing just his second game for Colorado, which posted its third consecutive victory to move into a first-place tie with Calgary in the Pacific Division.
